trial_court: Family Court, HMA Petition No. 262-S/3 of 2019/16
facts_of_case: Petitioner sought dissolution of marriage with respondent on ground of cruelty. Respondent left matrimonial house without intimation. A son was born out of wedlock.

legal_principles.principle: Cruelty may be mental or physical, intentional or unintentional.
legal_principles.held: The cruelty may be mental or physical. It may be intentional or unintentional.
cited_cases: Shobha Rani Vs. Madhukar Reddi, (1988) 1 SCC 105

legal_principles.principle: The impact of cruel treatment on the mind of the spouse must be considered.
legal_principles.held: Second, the impact of such treatment on the mind of the spouse. Whether it caused reasonable apprehension that it would be harmful or injurious to live with the other.
cited_cases: Shobha Rani Vs. Madhukar Reddi, (1988) 1 SCC 105

legal_principles.principle: Cruelty may not be established solely by the impact of the conduct, but also by the nature of the conduct itself.
legal_principles.held: There may, however, be cases where the conduct complained of itself is bad enough and per se unlawful or illegal. Then the impact or the injurious effect on the other spouse need not be enquired into or considered.
cited_cases: Shobha Rani Vs. Madhukar Reddi, (1988) 1 SCC 105

legal_principles.principle: The court should not import its own notions of life and should consider the type of life the parties are accustomed to.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, when a spouse makes complaint about the treatment of cruelty by the partner in life or relations, the court should not search for standard in life. A set of facts stigmatised as cruelty in one case may not be so in another case.
cited_cases: Shobha Rani Vs. Madhukar Reddi, (1988) 1 SCC 105

outcome.final_order: Order dated 09.09.2021 set aside and petition allowed.
